questions.correct: By running the left and right sides at different speeds
wrong: By turning a front wheel left or right like a car
By tilting the whole robot over toward one side
By spinning a single steering wheel in the center
questions.explain: Tank drive steers by speed difference: same speed both sides = straight, different = a turn, opposite = spin in place — like a bulldozer's two tracks.

questions.q: Why must the left motors be reversed?
questions.correct: The two sides are mirror images and would otherwise fight
wrong: The left motors are always weaker than the right ones
Reversing them makes the battery last much longer
The rules require the left side to run backward
questions.explain: Left and right motors face opposite ways (mirror images). Without reversing the left side, "forward" power would spin the two sides in opposite directions.

questions.q: How do you reverse a motor in code?
questions.explain: setDirection(DcMotor.Direction.REVERSE) flips which way a motor treats as forward — no rewiring needed. It's the clean way to mirror the left side.

questions.q: How do you look up a motor from the config?
questions.explain: hardwareMap.get(DcMotor.class, "name") finds a motor by its config name and hands it back. The name must match the robot configuration exactly.

questions.q: In tank drive, the LEFT power is...
questions.explain: Left power = drive + spin and right power = drive - spin. Adding spin on the left and subtracting on the right makes the sides differ, which turns the robot.

questions.q: In tank drive, the RIGHT power is...
questions.explain: Right power = drive - spin (left is drive + spin). The opposite spin terms on each side create the turn.

questions.correct: Stick up reads negative, so the sign is flipped
wrong: The stick reports numbers that are far too large
Negative power makes the motor much stronger
The minus sign turns off the stick deadzone
questions.explain: Up on the stick reads negative, but you want up to mean forward. The minus flips it so pushing up drives the robot forward.

questions.q: Why multiply the powers by 0.5 while learning?
questions.correct: To cap the robot at half speed for safety
wrong: To make the drive motors twice as strong
To reverse the left side of the robot
To convert the sticks into whole numbers
questions.explain: Multiplying by 0.5 keeps the robot at half speed while you learn, so it's easy to control. Bump it toward 1.0 once you're comfortable.

questions.correct: A value from -1.0 (full reverse) to 1.0 (full forward)
wrong: A value from 0 to 100, treated as a percent
Only true or false, meaning on or off
questions.explain: setPower takes -1.0 to 1.0. Negative is reverse, positive is forward, and 0 stops the motor.

questions.q: In tank drive, both left motors get...
questions.explain: Both left motors share one power and both right motors share another. That's what makes it tank drive — two sides, like two tracks.

questions.q: Where should the motor setup happen?
questions.correct: In init, once, before the run loop
wrong: Inside the loop, on every single pass
After the class's final closing brace
Inside an import line up at the top
questions.explain: Finding motors and setting directions is one-time setup, so it goes in init before waitForStart() — not inside the fast run loop.

questions.q: If the robot spins when you push straight forward...
questions.correct: The left motors probably weren't reversed
wrong: The battery is probably almost fully dead
The sticks are stuck inside the deadzone
The telemetry line is missing its label
questions.explain: A spin on "forward" is the classic sign the left side wasn't reversed — so the two sides push against each other. Check your setDirection calls.

questions.q: What does the spin value come from?
wrong: gamepad1.a, one of the face buttons
questions.explain: spin = gamepad1.left_stick_x (left/right), while drive = -gamepad1.left_stick_y (up/down). One controls turning, the other forward/back.

questions.q: Equal speed on both sides makes the robot...
questions.explain: Same speed both sides = straight. Different speeds = a gentle turn; opposite speeds = spin in place. That's how tank steering works.
setPower(0) sends zero power, so the motor stops. Positive spins forward, negative spins reverse.
